How is Missouri organized when you sell a house?

Missouri has 114 counties plus one independent city, St. Louis, which is not part of any county. The city's residents voted to leave St. Louis County in 1876, so a house inside city limits answers to city offices for several steps that a county office handles elsewhere.

St. Louis County is the most populous at about 990,911 people in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, while Worth County has about 1,914. Counties collect taxes, keep the roads and elect a sheriff, a prosecuting attorney and an assessor.

For a seller, the practical point is that state law sets the rules and the county sets the routine. Your recorder of deeds, assessor and collector each keep their own hours and forms. Our Missouri guides by city and county page lists every local guide we publish, and the county directory further down this page links the ones for your area.

What does a cash sale as-is mean in Missouri?

A cash sale as-is means the buyer pays without a mortgage and accepts the house in its current condition. You skip the repair list, the staging and the wait for a lender's appraisal.

It does not skip the paperwork. A title company still searches for liens, unpaid taxes and judgments. Missouri law requires a deed to be signed by the owner or an agent and acknowledged, and a written deed has to state whether each individual owner is married or unmarried.

A cash route tends to fit sellers who:

  • inherited a house they do not want to repair
  • are behind on a mortgage and need a firm closing date
  • own a rental with tenants still in place

Is there a transfer tax when you sell a house in Missouri?

No. Missouri does not charge a real estate transfer tax, according to HomeLight's state guide, so there is no state tax stamp on the deed. Other costs still exist, such as title fees, an unpaid homeowners association balance and the recording charge.

Recording is a county job. Under RSMo 59.310, a recorder of deeds may charge $5 for the first page of a deed and $3 for each page after that. Electronic filing is optional for recorders, so call yours first. We explain the steps in our Missouri recording a deed guide, and several recorder pages sit in the directory below.

Income tax on any gain is separate. See our Missouri capital gains tax page.

How do Missouri property taxes work for a seller?

Property tax in Missouri is set and collected locally, and the unpaid balance has to be cleared at closing. The title company will ask the county collector for the figure.

Under RSMo 137.115, residential real property is assessed at 19 percent of true value. Agricultural land is assessed at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent. Owners who disagree with a valuation can appeal first to the county Board of Equalization, then to the State Tax Commission.

ItemWhat the source says
Residential assessment rate19 percent of true value (RSMo 137.115)
Delinquent tax saleFourth Monday in August (RSMo 140.150)
Redemption after a tax saleOne year, with a continuing right until the buyer gets the deed (RSMo 140.340)

If taxes are behind, the date that matters most is the August sale. A lien can be discharged by sale, so an owner with delinquent taxes should talk to the county collector early. Our Missouri property tax guide walks through appeals and selling with tax due, and the city and county tax guides below cover local offices.

How does foreclosure work in Missouri?

Missouri lenders commonly sell through a power of sale written into the mortgage or deed of trust. RSMo 443.310 says such a sale must happen in the county where the land sits and must be advertised with not less than twenty days' notice.

That is a short window. An owner who has received a notice of sale can still sell before the auction, pay off the loan from the proceeds and keep any equity left.

Things to do if you have a sale notice:

  • Get a written payoff figure from the lender, including fees.
  • Ask the trustee for the date and place of the sale.
  • Compare any offer to the payoff before you sign.

If a house is sold at foreclosure with people still living in it, RSMo 534.030 lets the new owner start possession proceedings only after at least ten business days have passed from a written notice.

What happens to an inherited house in Missouri?

It depends on how title passes. A house left through a recorded transfer on death deed moves to the named beneficiary without probate, and our transfer on death deed guide explains that route. Without one, the estate usually goes through the probate division of the circuit court.

There is a shortcut for small estates. Under RSMo 473.097, distributees can take real property without waiting for letters if the whole estate, less liens, debts and encumbrances, does not exceed $40,000 and thirty days have passed since the death. The heirs file an affidavit with the probate clerk, and they record the affidavit and the clerk's certificate with the recorder of deeds in each county where the land sits.

Most family houses are worth more than $40,000, so a full estate is the common case. Our Missouri probate guide covers who inherits and who can sign the deed, and the Missouri estate tax page explains why heirs generally do not file a state estate tax return.

Does the Missouri homestead exemption help when you sell?

Not directly. The homestead statute, RSMo 513.475, protects a person's dwelling and the land used with it from attachment and execution by creditors, up to a dollar cap. The version posted on the Revisor of Statutes site shows a cap of $40,000 taking effect January 1, 2027.

That is a creditor protection rule, not a tax break at closing. The same section also says a spouse cannot sell or mortgage the homestead alone in the situations it describes, which is one reason title companies ask whether an owner is married. Property tax credits are a separate program, and our Missouri homestead exemption guide sorts the two apart.

What if the Missouri house has tenants?

A sale does not erase a lease, and a landlord still has to follow the statutes. A tenancy at will, or one for less than a year, can be ended with one month's written notice under RSMo 441.060. A month to month tenancy ends on a rent paying date at least a month after the tenant receives notice.

Deposits are capped at two months' rent under RSMo 535.300, and the landlord holds them in an insured bank or credit union. Within thirty days after the tenancy ends, the landlord owes an itemized list of deductions and the balance. A landlord who wrongfully keeps a deposit can owe the tenant twice the amount held back.

Our landlord tenant guide and eviction process page go through the steps in more detail.

What property problems do Missouri sellers run into?

Two hazards show up often in the state's own materials. The Department of Natural Resources describes Missouri as karst country, with more than 16,000 known sinkholes, more than 7,500 caves and more than 4,400 springs. If your house sits near a depression in the yard or a cracked foundation, say so early, because a buyer's inspector will look for it.

Radon is the other one. The Department of Health and Senior Services explains that radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas from the breakdown of uranium in soil, that it can build up indoors and that it raises lung cancer risk. The department also lists testing and mitigation pages for homeowners.

In an as-is cash sale you do not repair either problem first. Ask your county office or title company about any local disclosure form.

Who should you call before you list or sell?

Start with the county, then the title company. The recorder of deeds can tell you what a deed must contain, the county collector can give a tax balance, and the probate division of the circuit court can explain an open estate.

Inside St. Louis city those are city offices, because the city is not in a county. Kansas City reaches into Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass counties, so check the county on your tax bill. Browse the directory below to find your area.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Missouri have?

Missouri has 114 counties and one independent city, St. Louis, which is not inside any county.

Does Missouri charge a transfer tax on a home sale?

HomeLight reports no transfer tax. Recorders charge $5 for the first page and $3 for each added page (RSMo 59.310).

How much notice does a Missouri foreclosure sale require?

RSMo 443.310 requires not less than twenty days' notice for a sale under a power of sale, held in the county where the land sits.

Can I sell an inherited house in Missouri without probate?

Sometimes. A recorded transfer on death deed can pass it to a beneficiary, and an estate under $40,000 can skip letters after thirty days. Otherwise probate court is usually involved.

What is the residential assessment rate in Missouri?

RSMo 137.115 assesses residential real property at 19 percent of true value.

How much can a Missouri landlord hold as a security deposit?

No more than two months' rent under RSMo 535.300, with an itemized list of deductions due within thirty days after the tenancy ends.

Do I need to fix sinkholes or radon before a cash sale?

No repair is needed to sell as-is, but tell the buyer what you know. Missouri has more than 16,000 known sinkholes, and the state health department publishes radon information.

When is the Missouri delinquent tax sale?

RSMo 140.150 sets it for the fourth Monday in August.
